newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan tankan shows economic firmness strong-EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan tankan shows economic firmness strong-EPA.

text.p: Recent economic data, including the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) June "tanakan" corporate survey confirmed that the firmness of the Japanese economy was very strong, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya said on Friday.
Nukaya said the tankan results showed that there was a gap between the business confidence of large and smaller firms and between that of manufacturers and non-manufacturers.
But he added that such a gap, to a certain extent was unavoidable.
"Although we have such problems, recent economic indicators including the tankan confirmed that the economy's firmness is very strong," he said.

Nukaya said looking at the tankan result, capital spending for the April-June quarter looked strong although private consumption has been weak in reaction to the rise in the consumption tax on April 1.
But he said he believed strength in domestic demand was likely to continue during the April-June period.
Nukaya also said he expected industrial output for the April-June period to remain firm supported by strong exports.

The Trade Ministry said on Friday that May industrial output rose a preliminary 3.8 percent from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis. But the ministry forecast a 2.6 percent month-on-month fall for June.
On the unemployment rate, which rose to 3.5 percent in May, matching the record high marked in May and June of 1996, Nukaya said structural changes were a factor.
He said there was rise in a tendency among young people to seek a change of jobs and also an increase in women seeking new jobs.
